content.thinking: I should revise the root cause explanation so it doesn't call out a specific revision, and spell out each step in the chain individually rather than grouping them—noting specifically that U1 and U6 divide the figure while U2 and U3 simply read it. I also want to check whether the root cause's mention of the monthly statement, spend summary, and reconciliation reading the stored field might inadvertently trigger something.

action_items.item: Repair the stored month totals that fell behind, before the month rolls over. One way is to review and then run the repair script proposed in PR #344 against an export of the accounts and load the result back.
Once the fix in PR #344 is merged, deploy a revision that carries it, so the derive_the_month path in what runs also updates the month total.
Run the month-total reconciliation far more often than every {A5} days, or check the stored total against purchases on write.
Add a test to the deploy pipeline that writes purchases through every recording path and asserts the stored month total reconciles with the current-month purchases.
Require any revision deployed to io-shop to be in main's history.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to page the io-shop on-call.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored month-spend totals no longer matched their purchases. The spend-integrity check found {A1} of {A2} shopper totals that did not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}. Shopper-facing code uses that stored figure: the_mean_purchase_this_month in the monthly statement divides with it, _compared_with_usual and render_monthly_statement read it, and average_spend_per_item_this_month in the spend summary divides with it.

The stored total_this_month_cents was not updated when a current-month purchase was recorded. In the code that ran, record_purchase updates only total_cents. record_purchase_deriving_the_month also updates only total_cents. So whichever path record_a_purchase took, the purchase was added and the month total stayed where it was. reconcile_monthly_totals compares the field with the sum of the current-month purchases, and _the_disagreement_in subtracts the field from that sum.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 (revision 4c810f2). The alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after P2 at {P2.1}, and under P1's revision record_purchase still updated the month total.
A flag change setting it off. The flag provider showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T14.3} hour before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Deployment P2 at {P2.1} put a revision live that removed the month-total update from record_purchase. The diff against the previous revision shows the conditional addition to total_this_month_cents deleted, leaving only the total_cents addition. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running this revision.

The change dropped the stored month total on the premise, stated in the new docstring, that the month figure "adds up from the history whenever anybody wants it". The code that uses the field was not changed to match: the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month still divide with the stored field, and _compared_with_usual and render_monthly_statement still read it. With the writer no longer updating the stored copy, those figures came from a total that fell further behind with each current-month purchase.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop updating each shopper's stored spend total for the current month when they bought something, but the shop's statements and checks still use that stored total, so it fell behind what shoppers had actually bought.

contributing_factors.factor: The only check that compares stored month totals with purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs every {A5} days, and nothing in the write path notices a gap. The module's own docstring says nothing there notices when a total and the purchases disagree.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran far more often, or on write, would have flagged the gap soon after the deploy, not up to {A5} days later.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the deploy, no test or check was seen that the stored month total still reconciles with the purchases after writes through record_purchase on the revision that was deployed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have failed on the deployed revision and stopped the deploy.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The deployed revision is not in main's history, and nothing seen required a deployed revision to come from main.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The change would have had to pass whatever main's review and tests require before it ran.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told at once to roll back and repair the totals, instead of the action waiting as a recommendation.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

got_lucky: The alert fired in the same month the totals went wrong. A repair that recomputes the month total from current-month purchases is still possible. Once the month rolls over, that recomputed figure would be wrong.
went_well: Argus placed the onset just after the deploy, {T6.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and read the suspect deployment's diff {T10.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus checked the flag provider's history and found no flag change by anyone else before the onset, which narrowed the trigger to the deploy.
Code-Fix proposed a fix, new tests and a one-off repair script as draft PR #344, opened {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: Code-Fix wrote its fix against main, which does not contain the revision that ran, so the draft targets main's derive_the_month path and not the record_purchase change that actually ran.

input.root_cause: The deployed change removed the update of the stored per-shopper month total (total_this_month_cents) from record_purchase, assuming the month figure would be worked out from purchase history whenever it was needed. But the monthly statement and the spend summary still take that stored field, either reading it or dividing with it. The other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, also leaves the field unchanged. So every current-month purchase written since then left the stored month total further below the purchases behind it.
input.still_at_risk: The running code still leaves the stored month total unchanged on every current-month purchase, so the totals already written wrong stay wrong and keep falling further behind until somebody repairs them, and the repair has to happen before the month rolls over; also, the flag-selected path that derives the month (derive_the_month) leaves the total unchanged both in what ran and on main, so rolling back alone does not cover shoppers on that path.
input.symptom: Shoppers' stored spend totals for this month fell behind the purchases they had made
